text:
sarah_sales: Heads-up — MedSecure POC hit a burst of 5xxs during a demo 10m ago. They sent a heap of requests (~120 req/s) and saw intermittent 503/500 for ~2m. They’re nervous about SLA for the pilot. Can ops/eng triage?

miguel_support: On it. Do we have request_ids or an ingress log window? Which region/cluster?

sarah_sales: I grabbed the request IDs they reported: rq_8f3c2, rq_8f3c9, rq_8f3d1. Region: us-east-1, model: gptx-8k-quant (hosted), routing policy: burstpool enabled.

miguel_support: Thanks. @deploybot can you pull recent gateway traces for those ids and post autoscale events?

deploybot: Autoscale event: pool=burstpool-us-east-1, type=scale_up, start=1747654370, gpus_requested=4, worker_ready=1747654418, note="GPU init latency 48s".

miguel_support: Gateway log snippets for rq_8f3c2:
```
[1747654368] ingress: rq_8f3c2 received, routing->burstpool-us-east-1
[1747654369] pool: queueing request, active_workers=2, max_workers=2
[1747654371] error: 503 service_unavailable - no healthy backends
[1747654419] worker_ready: worker-7 registered
[1747654420] retry: routed to fallback-dedicated, success 200
```

alyssa_eng: Looks like classic autoscale cold-start: burstpool requested GPUs but workers weren't ready for ~48s. During that gap requests hit an empty pool and returned 503. We have automatic fallback to dedicated but that added latency and some requests timed out client-side.

alyssa_eng: Short-term mitigation: increase reserved min_workers for burstpool to 3 for this POC, or configure pre-warm on demo windows. Long-term: reduce GPU init coldstart via image slimming (working on a patch).

miguel_support: MedSecure also asked about burst pricing — they assume bursts are free with reserved. Can we confirm billing behavior? @sarah_sales please hold until I confirm.

sarah_sales: Yep, holding. Also they asked a security question re: logs — want to know if request payloads are stored in S3 and for how long.

miguel_support: Billing: burstpool minutes are billed as usage; reserved Dedicated capacity prevents queuing but burstpool is metered when used. See internal pricing note: https://redwood.internal/pricing#burstpool (I'll pull official quote).

miguel_support: Logs: request payloads are persisted for 30 days by default in debug mode; PII redaction can be enabled and retention shortened for enterprise. I'll attach a compliance snippet.

tim_oncall: I can flip burstpool min_workers to 3 for the MedSecure tenant now (will schedule a brief capacity bump). If they want immediate relief, I can also enable pre-warm for the next 30m demo window. Which do you want?

sarah_sales: Do both — bump min_workers to 3 and enable pre-warm for 30m. Tell me when done so I can update the customer.

tim_oncall: Doing now. Will post confirmation when applied.

miguel_support: Follow-up action items:
- @tim_oncall increase burstpool min_workers to 3 for MedSecure tenant (in progress)
- @alyssa_eng schedule image-slim patch to shave GPU init time (tracking: INF-2143)
- @miguel_support prepare short PRICING note and LOGS/compliance snippet for sales deck
- @sarah_sales update customer and request any replay logs if they still see 5xxs

sarah_sales: Thanks team — appreciate the quick swarm. I’ll ping if MedSecure wants us on the next demo.

deploybot: Action completed: update_config tenant=medsecure, pool=burstpool-us-east-1, min_workers=3 at 1747654930. Pre-warm enabled for 30m.

tim_oncall: Confirmed. Should reduce the chance of 5xxs during short spikes.

alyssa_eng: Note for postmortem: add metric for "gpu_init_time" in the autoscaler dashboard and alert if >30s during scale-up windows.

miguel_support: Closing this thread once pricing/compliance snippets are added to the case.

sarah_sales: Closing from sales side after customer update. :thumbsup:
